page: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-intel is a High Performance family cloud server featuring 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with 2 threads per core. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the x86_64 architecture processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 180 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a mix of average and weak performance profiles. Single-core processing is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1450.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1059.0, both falling into the average to weak categories. Multi-core performance is constrained, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 5759.17 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3411.0, which are classified as weak. Memory performance exhibits a similar split: cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 416.34 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to a weak 33.43 GB/sec. Cryptographic and database operations also show limitations, with a Passmark database score of 1279.7 and Redis SET operations performing at 6.06 million operations per second.

Given its shared CPU allocation and 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, this server offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads requiring NVMe storage but not sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is suitable for lightweight tasks such as basic text processing, small-scale software compilation, and low-traffic web serving. However, it is less suited for intensive multi-threaded applications, large-scale database operations, or complex LLM inference, where its shared CPU architecture and lower memory bandwidth present performance bottlenecks.
description: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-intel is a High Performance virtual server configured with 4 shared Intel Xeon vCPUs, 8.0 GB of RAM, and 180 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture at 2.0 GHz, it features AVX-512 instruction support. Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1450.08, but weak multi-core scaling, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 3411.0. Memory bandwidth is average for cached small blocks but drops significantly for larger, uncached blocks. This resource profile offers a cost-effective option for lightweight, non-continuous workloads. It is best suited for basic web serving, text processing, and minor development tasks, while intensive database operations and multi-threaded processing are limited by the shared CPU allocation and moderate memory throughput.
